summary: Process switch `review_loop` decides how a review loop treats the findings a review returns. It ships at `current`, so every review runs as before, until a project sets `blocking_delta` in its Process Policy or a later release promotes it after at least 5 reviewed documents across at least 2 flows. At `blocking_delta`, only a critical or major finding starts a round in the backlog, Solution Design, Design System and Operation contract reviews and in Delivery code review. A minor finding is fixed only in a writer pass that already carries a blocking fix; otherwise it becomes a follow-up with an owner role and a revisit trigger. An Operation contract records it in an optional `Accepted Minor Findings` section that `operation_compile.py` validates like the backlog table, and a contract without the section checks as before. A code review minor carries its file, description, owner role and revisit trigger in the code review result, `approve-item-evidence` copies the open ones into the Item's code review record and `approve-review` lists them in the Delivery Review. A re-review reads only the open blocking findings, the diff between the reviewed and the fixed revision and its dependency context, and no clean extra round runs.
